ayeaye: An aye-aye, a strange lemur sitting upright on a bare branch, with shaggy black-brown fur, huge round orange staring eyes, prominent rodent front teeth and round thin dark ears as big as its own face. LOOK AT ITS HAND: it is a normal five-fingered hand gripping the branch, and ONE OF THOSE FIVE FINGERS - the middle one - IS FAR LONGER AND VASTLY THINNER THAN THE OTHER FOUR, a bare wiry skeletal finger of skin and bone with a small claw, growing from the same knuckle as its neighbours and clearly part of the same hand, bending at its own joints. It is a finger, attached, one of five, NOT a twig, NOT a stick, NOT a wand, NOT a separate object, and the animal is holding nothing at all. Four ordinary limbs, no wings, no membrane. Exactly one long bushy tail
baskingshark: A colossal harmless plankton-eating fish drifting slowly with its jaws opened to their fullest, seen from a THREE-QUARTER FRONT ANGLE so we look partly into the opening and partly along the grey-brown flank. The opening is a huge rounded funnel. WHERE THE UPPER AND LOWER JAW MEET, ALL THE WAY AROUND, THERE IS A SMOOTH CONTINUOUS PALE GREY GUM LINE - a soft even band of bare skin like the rolled rim of a rubber boot or the lip of a bathtub, completely smooth and unbroken along its whole length, with a plain uninterrupted outline. NOTHING GROWS ANYWHERE ALONG THAT GUM LINE, which is bare and blank and rounded. Set DEEP INSIDE the dark funnel, far back near the throat and well away from the rim, hang pale cream fibrous combs like curtains of frayed rope. Five enormous gill slits wrap the head like stacked collars, a short blunt nose above the opening, small dark eyes far out at the sides, a bulky body, a tall triangular fin, a crescent tail
sunfishmola: An ocean sunfish in STRICT SIDE PROFILE, side-on to the viewer, mouth at the front on the left, one round eye on the side of its head. THINK OF IT AS AN ENORMOUS FISH HEAD WITH NO BODY BEHIND IT: it looks exactly as though a gigantic fish has been CUT THROUGH VERTICALLY JUST BEHIND THE GILLS and everything behind that cut simply thrown away, leaving only the head - so the animal is one huge rounded silver-grey plate, as DEEP FROM BACK TO BELLY AS IT IS LONG FROM MOUTH TO CUT, standing on edge like a millstone or a car wheel. Its whole outline is a circle. The cut edge at the back is finished with a short WAVY SCALLOPED FRILL of skin lying flat against it like the crimped rim of a pie, and beyond that frill there is nothing whatsoever - the animal simply stops. From the TOP of the circle one enormous pointed fin rises straight UP and from the BOTTOM an identical one points straight DOWN, and these two are the only large fins. Rough mottled silver-grey hide, small pectoral fins, a tiny round mouth
blackrhino_c: A newborn rhinoceros calf only a few weeks old, seen from a THREE-QUARTER FRONT ANGLE with its head turned toward the viewer. Everything about it is babyish: a head far too big for its body, short stubby legs, a plump rounded barrel body, big soft dark eyes and enormous soft rounded ears. ITS FACE IN PROFILE IS ONE SMOOTH UNBROKEN CURVE FROM EARS TO LIP, exactly like the soft rounded muzzle of a Labrador puppy or a young hippopotamus - the entire top surface of its snout is bare, smooth, blank, rounded skin, gently domed, with a completely plain and even outline all the way along, and the silhouette of its face is a simple continuous arc with no shape breaking that line anywhere. At the very end of the snout, a pointed hooked prehensile upper lip for browsing. Soft mid-grey hide with a few gentle folds, evenly and softly lit, a stubby tufted tail
